limitations: A name built at runtime cannot be followed, so an empty impact list is not proof that nothing depends on the target.
A name match is lexical and whole-word. A local variable that happens to share the name is reported as a code_reference.
A node path built dynamically or stored in a variable cannot be followed; node-path results cover only static serialized paths and direct code literals.
A path a script builds at runtime cannot be followed, so an asset in use may still be listed as an orphan.
Files under res://addons/ are third-party and are not counted as orphans by default. excluded_addon_orphans says how many were left out; pass include_addon_orphans to see them.

A signal is reported as dead only when no file emits it, connects to it, or wires it in a scene. A connection made through a variable name cannot be seen, and neither can a member call written with the name and the .connect on different lines.

broken_connections reports only what it can prove. A connection whose receiving node sits inside an instanced or inherited scene, has a built-in or non-GDScript script, or extends something outside the project or the class reference is not judged, so an empty list is not a promise that every connection resolves.

source_changed_since_import and output_changed_since_import compare the source and the outputs against the source_md5 and dest_md5 Godot recorded in the .md5 it wrote beside the output. Those are two of the three questions the engine asks; it also checks the importer's version, which is not checked here, so no finding is not a promise that Godot will leave the asset alone. import_freshness_unchecked says a record is there and a half of it was not compared, and its detail says which half and why. source_newer_than_output is the fallback where there is no record at all: it compares modification times, which a clone, a checkout or a worktree does not preserve, so it is evidence rather than a verdict, and the remedy is to open the project in the editor once so a record exists.

project_settings_issues reports the three states of project.godot that a reader can see without the engine: a file that ends part-way through a value, a value the parser cannot start, and a setting registered under a name the join built. It is not a full parse, so a constructor with the wrong arity, one the engine does not know, and a Resource() whose file is missing are all ERR_PARSE_ERROR and none of them is reported. An empty list is not a promise that Godot will load the file; a finding is a promise that it will not.

initialize.instructions:
Didi: Godot project inspection and controlled editor/game operations.

DISCOVERY AND EXECUTION
Select the project with --project or DIDI_PROJECT_ROOT. Before invoking any tool, inspect tools/list: read its inputSchema, required parameters, descriptions, bounds, and _meta.didi availability. Use canonical names below; never invent tool names or parameters. Require implemented=true; live-only calls need currentMode=live or liveAvailable=true. Recheck discovery after session changes. Use runtime_list_sessions, runtime_attach_session, and runtime_get_session to select and verify the intended project and editor/game route. Check execution_mode and session_kind in results; offline_fallback is not observed or unsaved editor state.
Never brute-force node paths or probe guessed node names. Discover the hierarchy first, reuse returned paths, and refresh the relevant branch after structural changes or a missing-node error. Inspect errors and limitations before changing the request; do not repeat unsupported calls.
Preview mutations with the exact arguments plus dry_run=true; inspect mutation_preview and the project/route. If confirmation_token is returned, execute the same arguments without dry_run and with that token only after destructive intent is authorized. Do not replay uncertain mutations. Use editor_save_scene when scene persistence is intended.

TOOL ROUTING
- Files: project_list_resources discovers project paths; project_search_text finds literal text; project_search_symbols finds lexical GDScript/C# declarations.
- Scene tree: scene_get_hierarchy(root_path, max_depth, max_nodes) returns names, classes, paths, and children. Start bounded or use summary=true; inspect truncation and expand only relevant branches. A .tscn root_path reads the saved file even when attached. Live bulk properties, scripts, and signals are omitted; inspect omitted_fields.
- Node properties: scene_get_property(target_node, property_name) reads an existing property on a discovered live node, with its declared type; scene_set_property writes it. property_name may be a path into a resource the node holds, a colon before each step. A batch of writes is one undo step. Do not infer all properties from the hierarchy.
- Project settings: project_get_setting(setting) reads a value; project_set_setting writes it. Use project_list_autoloads/project_set_autoload for autoloads and the advertised InputMap tools for input/*, not project_set_setting for those namespaces.
- GDScript: script_get_symbols extracts declarations; script_check_syntax(file_path) attempts Godot compiler diagnostics. source_text alone is lexical checking, not proof of compilation: inspect engine_checked and limitation. project_verify_changes checks proposed files together in an isolated copy. script_reflect_class is a limited offline reference, not full live ClassDB or a language server.

BOUNDARIES AND FALLBACKS
Didi does not implement a real-time renderer or gameplay loop; Godot owns both. viewport_capture_frame provides snapshots (check is_live_frame); runtime_launch runs Godot and the advertised runtime tools offer bounded session controls, not arbitrary continuous gameplay automation. Didi is not a general shell, unrestricted GDScript executor, or binary asset editor; eval_gdscript is a restricted read-only expression language. resource_inspect reports metadata/dependencies, not arbitrary Resource internals.
For source details beyond tool output, inspect the selected project's .tscn/.gd files directly (and project.godot for saved configuration); files cannot reveal unsaved or runtime state. For compiler or execution checks beyond supported tools, use godot --headless with the explicit project path and appropriate check/test options. Headless checks do not validate real-time rendered appearance. Use Godot/import tooling for binary assets. Registered but unimplemented tools are not capabilities: do not call physics_simulate_step, nav_bake_mesh, or runtime_get_call_stack while discovery marks them unimplemented.

asset_configure_import.description: Changes an imported asset's import options in its .import file, reimports it in the attached editor, and checks what the engine then loads. This is how a music track is made to loop: loop: true for an OGG or MP3, edit/loop_mode 2 (Forward) for a WAV. It sets the loop options of WAV, OGG and MP3 imports only, and refuses any other importer or option. Godot checks none of these values, so the tool does: a value of the wrong type, a loop mode Godot has no name for, an offset or a loop window outside the track. If the reimported asset does not load with what was asked, the previous file is put back and reimported. resource_inspect reports an asset's current import options.

asset_path.description: The imported asset whose options change, such as res://music/menu.ogg, as it is spelled on disk. It must already have its .import file; asset_reimport imports a new asset first.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

options.description: The import options to set and their new values. An OGG or MP3 takes loop and loop_offset, a WAV edit/loop_mode, edit/loop_begin and edit/loop_end. Every other key is refused, naming the ones this asset's importer takes.

edit/loop_begin.description: WAV: the first frame of the loop, under loop modes 2 to 4.

edit/loop_end.description: WAV: the frame the loop ends at, or -1 for the last one, under loop modes 2 to 4.

edit/loop_mode.description: WAV: 0 Detect From WAV, 1 Disabled, 2 Forward, 3 Ping-Pong, 4 Backward, as the number or the name.

loop.description: OGG and MP3: whether the track loops.

loop_offset.description: OGG and MP3: the second the track loops back to, from 0 up to its length.

author.description: Who applied the patch. Recorded as metadata, never verified. The task tools call the same idea agent_id, because there it is an identity a lease is checked against rather than provenance.

board.description: Board name. Letters, digits, underscore and hyphen. Separate boards do not see each other.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

expected_revision.description: Only apply if the board is still at this revision, which every read and write returns. A patch spans paths, so its unit is the board rather than one key. A mismatch is refused 409 with reason_code stale_patch.

operations.description: RFC 6902 operations against the board root. If any one fails, none is applied and the board is unchanged.

reason.description: Why the change is being made. Stored with the entry.

blackboard_patch.name: blackboard_patch
blackboard_patch.title: Patch a blackboard

blackboard_read.description: Reads a board or a subtree of one. Deep returns the whole subtree; shallow returns one level and marks nested containers rather than dropping them.

board.description: Board name. Letters, digits, underscore and hyphen. Separate boards do not see each other.

deep.description: False returns one level, with nested containers replaced by a _truncated marker carrying their size.

include_metadata.description: Include the author, reason, write time and expiry recorded for each path.

path.description: Dot or slash path. Omit to read the whole board.

blackboard_read.name: blackboard_read
blackboard_read.title: Read from a blackboard

blackboard_task_claim.description: Atomically leases the next ready task, or a named one. Reading that a task is free and writing that it is yours happen under one lock, so two agents cannot both win it.

agent_id.description: Who is taking the work. Recorded as the lease owner and required to update or complete it.

board.description: Which board to claim from. Defaults to the default board.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

lease_seconds.description: How long the claim holds. When it lapses the task returns to the pool, so an agent that dies does not strand the work.

tag.description: Only consider tasks carrying this tag.

task_id.description: Claim this task specifically. Omit to take the highest priority ready one.

blackboard_task_claim.name: blackboard_task_claim
blackboard_task_claim.title: Claim a task

blackboard_task_complete.description: Marks a task done and releases whatever was waiting on it. Only the agent holding the live lease may complete it, because completing someone else's task releases dependents on work that is still half done.

artifacts.description: Free-form record of what changed: files, node paths, board keys. Stored and returned verbatim.

board.description: Which blackboard to read or write. Defaults to the default board, so a single-agent session never needs to pass it.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

task_id.description: The task to complete. Only the lease holder may, because completing someone else's releases its dependents on work that is still half done.

blackboard_task_complete.name: blackboard_task_complete
blackboard_task_complete.title: Complete a task

blackboard_task_create.description: Registers a unit of work on the board, optionally waiting on other tasks. A task whose prerequisites are unmet is blocked until every one of them completes.

assigned_to.description: A suggestion only. Claiming is what actually assigns work.

author.description: Who asked for this task, which is not who should do it. Recorded as metadata, never verified. The claim and update tools take agent_id instead, because there it is an identity the lease is checked against rather than provenance.

board.description: Which blackboard to read or write. Defaults to the default board, so a single-agent session never needs to pass it.

dependencies.description: Task ids that must reach completed first. Each must already exist: depending on something that does not exist would block forever with nothing to explain it.

description.description: What the task involves, for whoever claims it. At most 4096 characters, which is the maxLength this parameter publishes.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

priority.description: Higher is claimed first. Ties go to the older task.

tags.description: Labels to file the task under. blackboard_task_claim can claim by tag.

task_id.description: Letters, digits, underscore, hyphen and dot. Generated as TASK-n when omitted.

title.description: Short name for the task. At most 512 characters, which is the maxLength this parameter publishes.

blackboard_task_create.name: blackboard_task_create
blackboard_task_create.title: Create a task

blackboard_task_list.description: Lists tasks with their status, lease and dependencies, filtered by status, assignee or tag. Lapsed leases are reclaimed before the list is built, so nothing reads as held by an agent that is gone.

assigned_to.description: Keep only tasks held by this agent.

board.description: Which blackboard to read or write. Defaults to the default board, so a single-agent session never needs to pass it.

status.description: Keep only tasks in this state: pending, in_progress, blocked, needs_review, completed or failed. A claimed task is in_progress; there is no claimed state.

tag.description: Keep only tasks carrying this tag.

blackboard_task_list.name: blackboard_task_list
blackboard_task_list.title: List tasks

blackboard_task_update.description: Records progress, adds a note, renews the lease, or hands the task back for review. Requires the live lease, except for reopening a needs_review or failed task.

agent_id.description: Must hold the live lease, unless reopening a needs_review or failed task, which is by definition somebody else's call.

board.description: Which blackboard to read or write. Defaults to the default board, so a single-agent session never needs to pass it.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

note.description: Appended to the task's notes. The oldest is dropped past 100.

progress.description: How far along the task is, as a whole percentage. A completed task reports 100.

renew_lease_seconds.description: Push the lease expiry out. Nothing renews a lease on an agent's behalf.

status.description: needs_review and failed both release the lease. pending reopens a reviewed or failed task.

task_id.description: The task to update. Requires the live lease, except when reopening a needs_review or failed task, which is by definition somebody else's call.

blackboard_task_update.name: blackboard_task_update
blackboard_task_update.title: Update a task

blackboard_write.description: Writes a value at a dot or slash path on a shared board, so a later agent in another process can read the decision instead of re-deriving it.

author.description: Who wrote it. Recorded as metadata, never verified. The task tools call the same idea agent_id, because there it is an identity a lease is checked against rather than provenance.

board.description: Board name. Letters, digits, underscore and hyphen. Separate boards do not see each other.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

expected_updated_at_ms.description: Only write if the path is still at this updated_at_ms, which blackboard_read returns. 0 means the path must not exist yet. A mismatch is refused 409 with reason_code stale_write and the time it actually holds, the shape blackboard_task_claim already uses for a claim somebody else holds. Omit it for a last-writer-wins write.

path.description: Dot or slash path such as architecture.inventory.slots. Segments cannot be empty, '.' or '..'.

reason.description: Why it was written. Recorded as metadata.

ttl_seconds.description: Drop the entry once this many seconds have passed. Expiry is applied on the next read, listing or write.

value.description: Any JSON value. Stored and returned verbatim; Didi never interprets or executes it.

blackboard_write.name: blackboard_write
blackboard_write.title: Write to a blackboard

capture_viewport.description: Captures the active editor 2D/3D viewport as PNG when live, or returns an attributed synthetic grid preview offline. Legacy name for viewport_capture_frame, which is listed separately and is the same tool. Prefer the canonical name: it is what error data reports as canonical_tool.

camera_identifier.description: Which editor viewport to capture. The 3D names are active_editor_view, editor_3d, active_editor_view_3d and 3d; the 2D names are editor_2d, active_editor_view_2d, 2d and canvas_item. Editor sessions only.

isolation_background.description: What to put behind an isolated node: original, or transparent.

node_isolation_path.description: Name a node in the edited scene to capture it alone. Unrelated branches are hidden for the capture and restored afterwards. Editor sessions only.

render_debug_flags.description: Reserved. Debug draw flags are not honoured by capture; use viewport_toggle_debug_draw.

resolution.description: Offline preview size; reserved and ignored by live capture

select_main_screen.description: Select the editor main screen this camera_identifier belongs to before capturing, then put the previous one back. An editor viewport has no size unless its main screen is showing, so without this an unattended agent cannot capture one at all. Editor sessions only.

capture_viewport.name: capture_viewport
capture_viewport.title: Capture a viewport frame

create_visual_test_lab.description: Writes a basic offline sandbox .tscn at res://didi_test_lab.tscn with lighting, a ground box, and three cameras. A PackedScene target is instanced under the lab as TargetInstance; any other resource is attached to a TargetInstance holder as metadata/didi_target, and the result says which with target_instanced. Legacy name for viewport_create_test_lab, which is listed separately and is the same tool. Prefer the canonical name: it is what error data reports as canonical_tool.

camera_rig.description: Metadata only; generated scene contains front, top, and isometric cameras

confirmation_token.description: Single-use token from an exact dry-run preview when confirmation is required.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

environment.description: Which lighting environment the generated scene uses.

orthographic.description: Give the generated scene an orthographic camera instead of a perspective one.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing lab scene at that path. Off by default, and a call with overwrite: true is confirmation-gated.

target_resource_path.description: The res:// resource the generated lab scene puts on show. It must already exist.

create_visual_test_lab.name: create_visual_test_lab
create_visual_test_lab.title: Build the visual test lab

csharp_check_build.description: Runs a bounded dotnet build and returns structured C# compiler diagnostics.

configuration.description: Which MSBuild configuration to build: Debug or Release.

project_file.description: A normalized project-contained .sln or .csproj to build. When omitted, exactly one of either must sit at the project root, and a .sln there is built in preference to a .csproj beside it. The answer's project_file names the one that was built.

request_id.description: Runs the call as a job; repeating it with this request_id reads the result.

timeout_seconds.description: How long the build may take before it is abandoned, in seconds.

csharp_check_build.name: csharp_check_build
csharp_check_build.title: Build the C# project

didi_control_room.description: Reports Didi's own state: bridge and session status with the pid or session behind it, the current execution mode of every registered tool, the safety posture, and a tail of this server's log. Read-only. Hosts that support the MCP Apps extension render it as an interactive dashboard; every other client gets the same payload as text.

fields.description: Sections to return. The others are left out and named in omitted_fields. Omit for every section.

log_limit.description: How many of the newest log records to return. The default is a glance; ask for more only when a person is going to read them.

didi_control_room.name: didi_control_room
didi_control_room.title: Open the control room

editor_clear_ghost_previews.description: Removes wireframe previews from the editor viewport. With no argument it clears every preview, which is the call that works whatever left them behind.

preview_id.description: Clear just this batch. Omit to clear all of them.

editor_clear_ghost_previews.name: editor_clear_ghost_previews
editor_clear_ghost_previews.title: Clear ghost previews

editor_redo.description: Replays the previously reverted editor transaction.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

editor_redo.name: editor_redo
editor_redo.title: Redo in the editor

editor_reload_project.description: Runs a full EditorFileSystem.scan in the connected editor and answers once it is applied; request_id waits as a job. Not a restart: a resource the editor has loaded is not reloaded.

confirmation_token.description: Single-use token from an exact dry-run preview when confirmation is required.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

request_id.description: Runs the call as a job; repeating it with this request_id reads the result.

editor_reload_project.name: editor_reload_project
editor_reload_project.title: Reload the project

editor_render_ghost_preview.description: Draws translucent wireframe boxes in the open editor viewport to show where a proposed mutation would land, without adding anything to the scene, so the scene never becomes dirty and there is nothing to undo.

previews.description: Shapes to draw. All of them share one dimension, because a 2D rectangle and a 3D box are drawn into different worlds.

color.description: Overrides the colour the kind would pick. Components r, g and b from 0 to 1.

kind.description: Chooses the colour: cyan for an addition, yellow for a translation, red for a deletion.

label.description: Echoed back so a caller can tell one shape from another. It is not drawn.

position.description: Centre of the shape: {x,y} for 2D or {x,y,z} for 3D.

rotation_degrees.description: 3D only: {x,y,z} Euler degrees. A 2D preview is an axis-aligned rectangle.

size.description: Full extents, the size a person would type into the inspector. Every axis must be greater than 0.

replace.description: Clear the previews already on screen first. A preview usually stands for one proposal, so replacing is the default.

editor_render_ghost_preview.name: editor_render_ghost_preview
editor_render_ghost_preview.title: Draw a ghost preview

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

editor_save_scene.name: editor_save_scene

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

editor_undo.title: Undo in the editor

eval_gdscript.description: Evaluates a bounded read-only GDScript expression in the active runtime session.

context_node.description: The node the expression's `node` is bound to. Read a native property of it with node.get("position"); reading through an object with node.position is refused, because that can run a script getter. Defaults to the edited-scene root for an editor and the running scene root for a game. Optional in-subtree canonical NodePath; server enforces a 1024-byte UTF-8 cap

expression.description: Read-only expression; server enforces a 2048-byte UTF-8 cap

timeout_ms.description: How long the expression may run before it is abandoned.

eval_gdscript.name: eval_gdscript
eval_gdscript.title: Evaluate GDScript

execute_test_session.description: Starts a separate Godot process. Blocking by default: captures stdout/stderr, classifies errors after exit, and enforces a 1-120 second timeout. With detach: true it leaves the game running and answers with the session to drive it through. Legacy name for runtime_launch, which is listed separately and is the same tool. Prefer the canonical name: it is what error data reports as canonical_tool.

break_on_error.description: Classify captured ERROR lines as failure after process exit; does not terminate the child early

detach.description: Leave the game running and return once it has published a session. Nothing is captured: read it with runtime_read_output and end it with runtime_stop.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

extra_args.description: Extra command-line arguments passed to the engine.

fixed_fps.description: true for the project's tick rate, or 1 to 1000, so each stepped frame is one physics tick. Unpaused, it runs as fast as it can.

headless.description: Run without a window. The engine still runs project code.

scene_path.description: The res:// scene to run. Defaults to the project's main scene.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait for the session to come up before giving up.

execute_test_session.name: execute_test_session
execute_test_session.title: Run the project

get_scene_hierarchy.description: Returns a live name/type/path hierarchy or an offline parsed .tscn hierarchy; live bulk properties, scripts, and signals are explicitly omitted. Legacy name for scene_get_hierarchy, which is listed separately and is the same tool. Prefer the canonical name: it is what error data reports as canonical_tool.

class_filter.description: Keep only nodes of these types and the ancestors that lead to them. Matches are flagged with matched: true.

include_properties.description: Include each node's property values when reading a .tscn file. The live editor route never returns bulk properties, so this has no effect there and bulk_properties is always named in omitted_fields.

max_depth.description: Stop descending below this depth. Branches that were cut report children_omitted and children_summary, and the response carries truncated.

max_nodes.description: Stop after this many nodes, depth first. Branches that were cut report children_omitted and children_summary.

root_path.description: Node path in the edited scene, or an in-project .tscn file path. A .tscn path is read from the file whether or not an editor is attached.

summary.description: Return node counts by type plus one level of branch structure, with no properties. Cannot be combined with max_nodes or class_filter.

get_scene_hierarchy.name: get_scene_hierarchy
get_scene_hierarchy.title: Read the scene tree

generate_collisions.description: Build collision shapes for each mesh in the library.

output_path.description: Where to write the generated MeshLibrary.

source_scene.description: The res:// scene whose children become the library's meshes. It must already exist.

timeout_seconds.description: How long the export may take before it is abandoned.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

navigation_layers.description: Navigation layers the path may use, as a 32-bit bit mask.

patch_script_symbols.description: Safely rewrites a single method or symbol body in a .gd file without touching other functions. Legacy name for script_patch_method, which is listed separately and is the same tool. Prefer the canonical name: it is what error data reports as canonical_tool.

from.description: Where the ray starts, as {x, y} or {x, y, z}. Both endpoints take the same number of dimensions and every coordinate must be finite.

project_add_export_preset.description: Adds one export preset to export_presets.cfg, which project_export needs and a project nobody has exported by hand does not have. It only adds: a name already in the file is refused. It writes the fewest keys every supported Godot loads cleanly and leaves the rest to the editor. dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

export_path.description: Where the editor's Export dialog proposes to write the build, relative to the project or as res://. Optional: project_export takes its own output_path either way. Stored relative to the project, the way the editor stores a path inside it.

max_impacts.description: Stop after this many impacts and report the result as truncated.

target.description: A canonical res:// path, lowercase-alphanumeric uid:// value, static Godot node path such as Player/Sprite, /root, or Hand/Sword/%Hilt, or a single Godot identifier such as a variable, function, or signal name.

project_analyze_impact.name: project_analyze_impact

changes.description: The proposal. The same shape project_verify_changes takes, checked the same way before any of it reaches the working tree.

content.description: The whole proposed contents of that file, at most 1 MiB.

path.description: A res:// path inside the project. The same containment rules script_create applies.

confirmation_token.description: Single-use token from an exact dry-run preview when confirmation is required.

discard_unsaved.description: Allow reloading an open tab that may hold unsaved edits.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

run_frames.description: Iterations to let the scene run before Godot quits by itself. Only meaningful with run_scene.

run_scene.description: Optional. A .tscn or .scn to open in the copy before deciding, so a scene that fails to load stops the write.

timeout_seconds.description: How long the verification run may take before the apply is abandoned.

project_apply_changes.name: project_apply_changes
project_apply_changes.title: Apply a verified change set

include_broken_connections.description: Scene [connection] entries whose method the receiving node's script, the scripts it extends and its engine class do not declare. Judged only where every step resolves.

include_broken_references.description: res:// paths and uid:// references that resolve to no file in the project.

include_dead_signals.description: Signals declared in GDScript that no file emits, connects to, or wires in a scene.

include_import_health.description: Existing Godot .import metadata with missing sources or outputs, malformed/unsafe paths, or source files newer than their outputs.

include_orphans.description: Assets that nothing references. Asset types only: scenes and scripts are excluded because nothing has to reference the level you open by hand.

max_findings.description: Stop after this many findings and report the result as truncated.

project_audit_assets.name: project_audit_assets

resource_create.description: Writes textual .tres content under the project root. Every value is rendered as a Godot literal or the call is refused naming the property, so a resource is never reported as written when part of it was thrown away. With an editor attached, the editor's copy of the file is reloaded from what was written.

allow_unknown_type.description: Write a resource_type that no engine list and no project class_name names. Off by default, because Godot cannot load a resource whose type it does not know and a misspelling is the common case. Turn it on for a GDExtension type with no session attached; an attached engine's ClassDB already lists one. The result then reports property_check as unchecked, or type_unknown_to_attached_engine and a limitation when the engine answered and does not have the type.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

overwrite.description: Replace the file when one is already at that path. Off by default, and a call with overwrite: true is confirmation-gated: dry-run it first and repeat the call with the token that comes back.

properties.description: An object, whose keys are written in sorted order, or an array of {name, value} entries written in the order given. Use the array when order matters: Godot applies indexed sub-properties in file order, so tracks/0/type has to come before the rest of track 0. A value is a string, number, boolean, array, or an object. An object with x/y, x/y/z, x/y/z/w or r/g/b(/a) numbers becomes whichever Vector or Color the property is declared as, and the matching one by shape when the class reference does not carry the property; any other object is a Dictionary. So tile_size on a TileSet takes {x, y} and is written Vector2i, and a fractional component in an integer vector is refused rather than truncated. To choose the type yourself, give the object a "type": Vector2i, Vector3i, Vector4i, Quaternion and Color take their components; NodePath and StringName take their text under "value"; the packed arrays take their elements under "values", and the composite ones -- PackedVector2Array, PackedVector3Array, PackedVector4Array and PackedColorArray -- take either an element per entry or the components already flattened, which is Godot's own format. The declared type also decides what kind of value the slot takes: int a whole number, float a number, bool true or false, String, StringName and NodePath a string, Array and the packed arrays an array, and Color either components or a "#rrggbbaa" string. Anything else is refused, because Godot keeps the property's default for a value it cannot convert and says nothing. A property can also point at another resource: {"type": "ExtResource", "path": "res://art/tiles.png"} references a file in the project, and {"type": "SubResource", "id": "Atlas_1"} references an entry of sub_resources declared above it. A type this cannot write is refused rather than guessed at.

resource_type.description: The Godot class to write into the [gd_resource] header, such as CanvasItemMaterial, or a project script's class_name, written as its engine base with the script set. A name neither the engine nor a script has is refused, because Godot cannot load a resource whose type it does not know. With a session attached that is the attached engine's own ClassDB, not the pinned 4.7 reference, which has 65 classes 4.5.1 lacks. Pass allow_unknown_type for a GDExtension type.

save_path.description: Target res:// path ending in .tres. A .res is Godot's binary format and is refused.

sub_resources.description: The [sub_resource] blocks this resource carries inside itself, in the order they should appear. Each entry is {id, resource_type, properties}, and its properties follow exactly the same rules as the top-level ones. A property anywhere in the file names one with {"type": "SubResource", "id": ...}, and only an id declared earlier can be named, because Godot resolves a SubResource against what it has already read. load_steps is computed from these and the external references; do not pass it.

A paused game is refused rather than explored, because a paused tree queues injected input instead of delivering it and the stillness would be the pause rather than the game.

A probe that never returns a value is listed in unread_probes and sets measured to false.

arguments.description: Positional arguments. JSON null, booleans, integers, finite reals, strings, arrays and string-keyed dictionaries, nested at most 4 levels and 8 KiB in total. The count and each type must match what the script declares.

confirmation_token.description: Single-use token from an exact dry-run preview when confirmation is required.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

method_name.description: A method the node's script declares. Names beginning with an underscore are refused: that is Godot's mark for an engine callback or a private helper.

target_node.description: Node path inside the active edited scene.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait when the method turns out to be a coroutine. A timeout reports that it was still running rather than claiming a result.

scene_call_method.name: scene_call_method
scene_call_method.title: Call a method on a node

scene_close.description: Closes the active scene, refusing when unsaved changes are reported or cannot be ruled out.

discard_unsaved.description: Close without checking. Required where the engine cannot report dirty state (before Godot 4.7), where the scene has never been saved, or where the engine reports it as unsaved. Results carry dirty_state_readable and dirty_state.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

scene_close.name: scene_close
scene_close.title: Close an open scene

scene_create.description: Creates, saves, and opens an empty Node2D, Node3D, or Control scene.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

overwrite.description: Replace the file when one is already at that path. Off by default, and a call with overwrite: true is confirmation-gated: dry-run it first and repeat the call with the token that comes back.

root_name.description: Name for the root node. Defaults to a name derived from the file.

root_type.description: Any Godot class that inherits Node, the same set scene_instantiate_node takes: CharacterBody2D for a player, Area2D for a pickup, CanvasLayer for a HUD. A class the engine does not know, or one that is not a Node, is refused naming it.

scene_path.description: Where to write the new scene, a normalized res:// path ending in .tscn. This is the output path; the argument is scene_path.

scene_create.name: scene_create
scene_create.title: Create a scene

scene_duplicate_node.description: Duplicates an existing node branch with unique names.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

target_node.description: Target NodePath to duplicate

scene_duplicate_node.name: scene_duplicate_node
scene_duplicate_node.title: Duplicate a node

scene_get_group_members.description: Returns edited-scene-confined members of a group.

group.description: The group to list members of. The answer also carries known_groups, the names any node in the edited scene is actually in, so a mistyped name is recoverable.

scene_get_group_members.name: scene_get_group_members
scene_get_group_members.title: List a group's members

scene_get_hierarchy.description: Returns a live name/type/path hierarchy or an offline parsed .tscn hierarchy; live bulk properties, scripts, and signals are explicitly omitted.

class_filter.description: Keep only nodes of these types and the ancestors that lead to them. Matches are flagged with matched: true.

include_properties.description: Include each node's property values when reading a .tscn file. The live editor route never returns bulk properties, so this has no effect there and bulk_properties is always named in omitted_fields.

max_depth.description: Stop descending below this depth. Branches that were cut report children_omitted and children_summary, and the response carries truncated.

max_nodes.description: Stop after this many nodes, depth first. Branches that were cut report children_omitted and children_summary.

root_path.description: Node path in the edited scene, or an in-project .tscn file path. A .tscn path is read from the file whether or not an editor is attached.

summary.description: Return node counts by type plus one level of branch structure, with no properties. Cannot be combined with max_nodes or class_filter.

scene_get_hierarchy.name: scene_get_hierarchy
scene_get_hierarchy.title: Read the scene tree

scene_get_property.description: Returns a node property from the live edited scene, with its declared type and any range, enum or resource type the engine declares.

property_name.description: Property name, or a path such as theme_override_styles/panel:bg_color

reads.description: Instead of the two above: several reads, answered in order.

target_node.description: Target NodePath

scene_get_property.name: scene_get_property
scene_get_property.title: Read a node property

scene_get_selection.description: Reports the nodes selected in the Godot editor, which is what a person means by "this node". Live and editor only: a selection exists only in a running editor.
scene_get_selection.name: scene_get_selection
scene_get_selection.title: Read the editor selection

scene_instantiate_node.description: Creates a built-in ClassDB node, or an instance of a packed scene, in the active edited scene with UndoRedo.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

node_type.description: Built-in ClassDB Node type to instantiate. One of node_type or scene_path is required; there is no default, because an empty request must not add a node. Ignored when scene_path is given: the instance is whatever the scene's root is, and the result reports its class.

parent_path.description: Where to put the new node. Defaults to the edited scene root.

properties.description: Initial property values, keyed by property name. Each value takes the JSON type matching the property on the new node: number for float (1.0, not "1.0"), integer for int, boolean for bool, string for String/StringName/NodePath, null for nil, {x,y} or {x,y,z} for Vector2/Vector2i/Vector3/Vector3i, {r,g,b} with optional a or a "#rrggbb" string for Color, a res:// path for a Resource slot, and an array or object for an Array or Dictionary.

scene_path.description: A res:// .tscn to instance instead of constructing a type, as the editor does when a scene is dropped into the tree. What the scene file records is an instance of that scene, not a copy of its nodes.

scene_instantiate_node.name: scene_instantiate_node
scene_instantiate_node.title: Add a node

scene_list_groups.description: Lists the groups assigned to a live edited-scene node.

target_node.description: Path to the node in the active edited scene this acts on, such as /root/Main/Player. The argument is target_node, not node_path.

scene_list_groups.name: scene_list_groups
scene_list_groups.title: List scene groups

scene_open.description: Opens or switches to an existing PackedScene in the editor.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

scene_path.description: The res:// .tscn to open as the edited scene. Every later scene_* call answers about this scene until another is opened.

scene_open.name: scene_open
scene_open.title: Open a scene

scene_pack_branch.description: Packs a duplicated live branch into a reusable PackedScene resource.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

overwrite.description: Replace the file when one is already at that path. Off by default, and a call with overwrite: true is confirmation-gated: dry-run it first and repeat the call with the token that comes back.

scene_path.description: Where to write the packed scene, a res:// path ending in .tscn. This is the output path; the argument is scene_path.

target_node.description: The branch to pack. This node becomes the root of the written scene.

scene_pack_branch.name: scene_pack_branch
scene_pack_branch.title: Pack a branch into a scene

scene_remove_from_group.description: Removes a live node from a group through UndoRedo.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

group.description: Group name, without path separators. Groups are Godot's own tagging, and a node can be in any number of them.

target_node.description: Path to the node in the active edited scene this acts on, such as /root/Main/Player. The argument is target_node, not node_path.

scene_remove_from_group.name: scene_remove_from_group
scene_remove_from_group.title: Remove a node from a group

scene_remove_node.description: Detaches a node through UndoRedo while retaining its lifetime for undo and redo.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

target_node.description: NodePath of target node

scene_remove_node.name: scene_remove_node
scene_remove_node.title: Remove a node

scene_reparent_node.description: Moves a node to a new parent while preserving global transforms.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

keep_global_transform.description: Keep the node where it looks like it is, adjusting its local transform to compensate for the new parent. On by default.

target_node.description: NodePath to reparent

scene_reparent_node.name: scene_reparent_node
scene_reparent_node.title: Reparent a node

scene_set_property.description: Sets an existing node property through UndoRedo with strict JSON/Godot type compatibility. The property is read back after the commit, so value is what it now holds. When applied is false, not_applied says why, with the range or enum the engine declares. writes sets several, on any nodes, as one undo step.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

make_unique.description: Write into copies of the resources the path enters, as Make Unique does.

property_name.description: Property name, or a path into a resource it holds: theme_override_styles/panel:bg_color, material:shader_parameter/tint

target_node.description: Target NodePath

value.description: New property value, as the JSON type matching the Godot property: number for float (1.0, not "1.0"), integer for int, boolean for bool, string for String/StringName/NodePath, null for nil, {x,y} or {x,y,z} for vectors (whole numbers for the integer ones), {r,g,b} with optional a or "#rrggbb" for Color, Godot's own members for the rest (Rect2 {position,size}, Transform3D {basis,origin}), an array for an Array or packed array, an object for a Dictionary, and a res:// path for a Resource slot (null clears it). A member the type does not have is refused.

writes.description: Instead of the three above: writes of the same shape, all checked first, then committed as one undo step. One that fails refuses the batch.

scene_set_property.name: scene_set_property
scene_set_property.title: Write a node property

script_attach_to_node.description: Attaches an existing Script resource to a live node through UndoRedo.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

script_path.description: The res:// script to attach. It must already exist; script_create writes one.

target_node.description: Path to the node in the active edited scene this acts on, such as /root/Main/Player. The argument is target_node, not node_path.

script_attach_to_node.name: script_attach_to_node
script_attach_to_node.title: Attach a script to a node

script_check_syntax.description: Checks GDScript with Didi's lexical rules and the open editor's language server, or for a file with no editor a headless Godot compile.

source_text.description: An unsaved buffer to check instead of the file at file_path. With no editor attached only the lexical rules run on it; limitation says so.

script_check_syntax.name: script_check_syntax
script_check_syntax.title: Check a script compiles

script_create.description: Writes a new GDScript file under the project root and returns the diagnostics for what it wrote.

confirmation_token.description: Single-use token from an exact dry-run preview when confirmation is required.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

overwrite.description: Replace the script when one is already at that path. Off by default, and a call with overwrite: true is confirmation-gated.

script_create.name: script_create
script_create.title: Create a script

script_detach_from_node.description: Detaches the current Script resource from a live node through UndoRedo.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

target_node.description: Path to the node in the active edited scene this acts on, such as /root/Main/Player. The argument is target_node, not node_path.

script_detach_from_node.name: script_detach_from_node
script_detach_from_node.title: Detach a script from a node

script_get_symbols.description: Extracts AST symbols, functions, signals, and typed variables from any script file.

max_symbols.description: Stop after this many declarations, counted across every kind, and report truncated. symbol_count_total says how many the file holds either way, so a clipped answer can be told from a complete one.

script_get_symbols.name: script_get_symbols
script_get_symbols.title: List a script's symbols

script_patch_method.description: Safely rewrites a single method or symbol body in a .gd file without touching other functions.

confirmation_token.description: Single-use token from an exact dry-run preview when confirmation is required.

create_if_missing.description: Add the symbol when the script does not declare it. Off by default: a patch names a symbol that is there, and appending one for a misspelt name leaves dead code beside the symbol you meant to edit. The result says which happened with created.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

new_definition.description: New method implementation. It has to declare the symbol named by method_name.

symbol_type.description: Which kind of symbol the name refers to: function, variable, constant, signal, enum or class. Defaults to function. Anything else is refused, because an unrecognised kind cannot be checked against the replacement.

script_patch_method.name: script_patch_method
script_patch_method.title: Patch a script symbol

script_reflect_class.description: Looks up a class in Didi's limited built-in offline reference map; this is not live ClassDB reflection.

fields.description: Sections to return. The others are left out and named in omitted_fields. Omit for every section.

script_reflect_class.name: script_reflect_class
script_reflect_class.title: Reflect an engine class

shader_check_compile.description: Loads one gdshader through bounded headless Godot and returns engine diagnostics.

timeout_seconds.description: How long the compile may take before it is abandoned.

shader_check_compile.name: shader_check_compile
shader_check_compile.title: Check a shader compiles

shader_get_visual_graph.description: Returns the nodes and connections of a VisualShader graph held by a node in the edited scene, per shader type, as structured JSON.

property_name.description: The property the ShaderMaterial sits in, the same pair shader_list_uniforms takes.

target_node.description: The node holding the VisualShader to read. A shader written as code rather than built as a graph is refused rather than answered with an empty node list.

shader_get_visual_graph.name: shader_get_visual_graph
shader_get_visual_graph.title: Read a visual shader graph

shader_list_uniforms.description: Reads the shader uniforms of a ShaderMaterial held by a node in the edited scene, with each uniform's declared type, its current value, and whether the material overrides it.

property_name.description: The property the ShaderMaterial sits in, such as material_override on a MeshInstance3D or material on a CanvasItem. Named rather than guessed; scene_get_property will say which properties a node has.

target_node.description: Node in the edited scene holding the material.

shader_list_uniforms.name: shader_list_uniforms
shader_list_uniforms.title: List shader uniforms

shader_set_uniform.description: Sets one shader uniform on a ShaderMaterial held by a node in the edited scene, through the editor UndoRedo stack, and reports what the uniform holds afterwards.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

property_name.description: The property the ShaderMaterial sits in, such as material_override.

target_node.description: The node holding the ShaderMaterial whose uniform to set.

uniform_name.description: Must be a uniform the shader declares. A name it does not know is refused rather than written and ignored.

value.description: The new value, in the same JSON spelling scene_set_property takes for that Godot type: a number for float, {x,y} or {x,y,z} for a vector, {r,g,b} with optional a or a "#rrggbb" string for a colour, and a res:// path for a texture or other resource uniform.

shader_set_uniform.name: shader_set_uniform
shader_set_uniform.title: Set a shader uniform

signal_connect.description: Binds a signal from an emitter node to a target method or callable.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

emitter_node.description: The node that emits the signal. The argument is emitter_node, not source_node.

flags.description: Godot connection flags, default 2. CONNECT_PERSIST is required and may be combined with CONNECT_DEFERRED and CONNECT_ONE_SHOT: 2, 3, 6 or 7, which is what the editor's Connect dialog writes. Add 32 and each is accepted again, because that is how signal_list_connections reports a connection inside an instanced scene and it is meant to be handed straight back. A value without CONNECT_PERSIST is refused: it would not be stored in the scene file, so it would vanish on reload and this tool would have reported work that did not last.

signal_name.description: The signal on the emitter to connect, as it is declared.

target_method.description: The method on the receiving node to call. The argument is target_method, not method_name, and the method must exist.

target_node.description: The node that receives the signal.

signal_connect.name: signal_connect
signal_connect.title: Connect a signal

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

emitter_node.description: The node that emits the signal. The argument is emitter_node, not source_node.

signal_name.description: The signal on the emitter to disconnect.

target_method.description: The method the connection currently calls. The argument is target_method, not method_name.

target_node.description: The node currently receiving the signal.

signal_emit.description: Emits a custom signal manually with arguments for event testing.

arguments.description: Positional values to emit with the signal. They must match the signal's declared parameters in count and type.

confirmation_token.description: Single-use token from an exact dry-run preview when confirmation is required.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

emitter_node.description: The node that emits the signal, as in signal_connect. target_node is accepted for the same node.

signal_name.description: The signal to emit, as the node declares it.

target_node.description: The same node as emitter_node, under the name this tool used first. Send one of the two.

signal_emit.name: signal_emit
signal_emit.title: Emit a signal

signal_list_connections.description: Lists the signals a node declares and the connections going out of each. The node is the emitter; connections into it are not listed.

emitter_node.description: The node whose own signals to list, with the connections going out of each: the emitter, as in signal_connect. Connections into this node are not listed. Each connection carries origin: scene for one inside the edited scene, editor for the scene dock's own listeners. target_node is accepted for the same node.

target_node.description: The same node as emitter_node, under the name this tool used first. Send one of the two.

signal_list_connections.name: signal_list_connections
signal_list_connections.title: List signal connections

spatial_query_clearance.description: Sweeps a box, sphere, or capsule along a path in the attached session's physics world and reports how far it gets, which is the question a doorway or a spawn point asks and a ray cannot answer.

collision_mask.description: Physics layers the shape is tested against, as a 32-bit bit mask.

shape.description: The body being fitted through. sphere is a circle in 2D.

size.description: box only: {x,y} or {x,y,z}, every component greater than 0.

to.description: Where the shape is sweeping to. Equal to from asks whether it fits where it stands.

spatial_query_clearance.name: spatial_query_clearance
spatial_query_clearance.title: Measure clearance around a point

spatial_query_frustum.description: Lists the 3D nodes inside a camera frustum in the attached session, nearest first, and can sample whether anything with a collider stands between the camera and each one.

camera.description: A frustum written out by hand. fov_degrees is vertical, matching a Godot camera's default.

aspect.description: Width over height. Required, because the frustum is a different shape without it.

look_at.description: {x,y,z} the camera points at, which must differ from position.

up.description: {x,y,z}. Defaults to {0,1,0}, and the value used is reported back.

camera_node.description: A Camera3D already in the scene, whose transform, projection, near and far planes are used. Exactly one of camera_node and camera is required.

collision_mask.description: Applies to the sightline rays only.

sightline.description: Sample rays from the camera to each node. Rays see physics colliders only, so geometry without one does not block.

spatial_query_frustum.name: spatial_query_frustum
spatial_query_frustum.title: Query the camera frustum

spatial_query_raycast_batch.description: Casts many rays against the attached session's physics world in one dispatch, sharing one space state, and returns the same hit record per ray that physics_raycast_query returns.

rays.description: Rays to cast. Every ray shares one dimension, because a 2D and a 3D ray are answered by different space states.

spatial_query_raycast_batch.name: spatial_query_raycast_batch
spatial_query_raycast_batch.title: Cast a batch of rays

tilemap_get_used_rect.description: Returns used cell boundaries and layer structures.

tilemap_path.description: The TileMapLayer to measure. A node that exists but is a different class is refused naming its actual class.

tilemap_get_used_rect.name: tilemap_get_used_rect
tilemap_get_used_rect.title: Read a tilemap's used area

tilemap_set_cells.description: Batch updates 2D TileMapLayer cells with source IDs, atlas coordinates, and alternate tiles.

cells.description: Records, each either a write or an erase and nothing else.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

tilemap_set_cells.name: tilemap_set_cells
tilemap_set_cells.title: Set tilemap cells

ui_hit_test.description: Hit-tests live Control nodes at a viewport-space point without injecting input. Editor or game: the edited scene in an editor, the running scene in a game.

include_mouse_filter_ignore.description: Include Controls set to MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE, which do not receive mouse input and are left out by default.

max_results.description: How many hits to return, ordered topmost first.

point.description: The point to test, as {x, y} in viewport coordinates.

root_path.description: Where to start looking. Defaults to the edited scene root in an editor and /root in a game; the answer reports the subtree it actually covered.

ui_hit_test.name: ui_hit_test
ui_hit_test.title: Find the control under a point

ui_list_controls.description: Lists live Control nodes under a root with each one's viewport-space rectangle, class, visibility, mouse filter and text. In a game, screen_rect is that rectangle in the window pixels runtime_inject_input takes. In a localised game text is the key; displayed_text, when it differs, is what the player reads. Read-only. ui_hit_test answers the opposite question: what sits under a point.

class_filter.description: Keep only Controls that are one of these classes, inheritance included.

include_text.description: Read the text property where the Control has one, and displayed_text where the Control draws it translated. Each is capped at 256 bytes.

root_path.description: Where to start. Defaults to the edited scene root in an editor and /root in a game.

visible_only.description: Skip Controls that are not visible in the tree, and everything beneath them.

ui_list_controls.name: ui_list_controls
ui_list_controls.title: List controls in a scene

viewport_capture_frame.description: Captures the active editor 2D/3D viewport as PNG when live, or returns an attributed synthetic grid preview offline.

camera_identifier.description: Which editor viewport to capture. The 3D names are active_editor_view, editor_3d, active_editor_view_3d and 3d; the 2D names are editor_2d, active_editor_view_2d, 2d and canvas_item. Editor sessions only.

isolation_background.description: What to put behind an isolated node: original, or transparent.

node_isolation_path.description: Name a node in the edited scene to capture it alone. Unrelated branches are hidden for the capture and restored afterwards. Editor sessions only.

render_debug_flags.description: Reserved. Debug draw flags are not honoured by capture; use viewport_toggle_debug_draw.

resolution.description: Offline preview size; reserved and ignored by live capture

select_main_screen.description: Select the editor main screen this camera_identifier belongs to before capturing, then put the previous one back. An editor viewport has no size unless its main screen is showing, so without this an unattended agent cannot capture one at all. Editor sessions only.

viewport_capture_frame.name: viewport_capture_frame
viewport_capture_frame.title: Capture a viewport frame

viewport_capture_passes.description: Draws the live 3D scene again with replacement materials and returns a depth or world-space normal image alongside the ordinary colour frame, so which thing is nearer and which way a surface faces can be read off the pixels rather than guessed.

camera_identifier.description: Editor sessions only; a game has one root viewport.

depth_far.description: The distance mapped to white in the depth pass. Defaults to the rendering camera's own far plane, and the value used is reported back.

passes.description: Which pictures to take, returned as one image each in this order. A pass named twice is refused.

select_main_screen.description: Select the editor main screen this camera_identifier belongs to before capturing, then put the previous one back. An editor viewport has no size unless its main screen is showing, so without this an unattended agent cannot capture one at all. Editor sessions only.

viewport_capture_passes.name: viewport_capture_passes
viewport_capture_passes.title: Capture render passes

viewport_create_test_lab.description: Writes a basic offline sandbox .tscn at res://didi_test_lab.tscn with lighting, a ground box, and three cameras. A PackedScene target is instanced under the lab as TargetInstance; any other resource is attached to a TargetInstance holder as metadata/didi_target, and the result says which with target_instanced.

camera_rig.description: Metadata only; generated scene contains front, top, and isometric cameras

confirmation_token.description: Single-use token from an exact dry-run preview when confirmation is required.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

environment.description: Which lighting environment the generated scene uses.

orthographic.description: Give the generated scene an orthographic camera instead of a perspective one.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing lab scene at that path. Off by default, and a call with overwrite: true is confirmation-gated.

target_resource_path.description: The res:// resource the generated lab scene puts on show. It must already exist.

viewport_create_test_lab.name: viewport_create_test_lab
viewport_create_test_lab.title: Build the visual test lab

viewport_diff_capture.description: Captures a fresh live editor viewport frame and returns an exact RGBA pixel diff against a prior process-local capture ID.

baseline_capture_id.description: The earlier capture to compare against, as that capture's result reported it.

camera_identifier.description: Which editor viewport to capture for the comparison. The same selector viewport_capture_frame takes.

isolation_background.description: What to put behind an isolated node: original, or transparent.

max_hamming_distance.description: Largest perceptual-hash distance that still counts as perceptually identical. Sets perceptually_identical in the result.

min_ssim.description: Structural similarity at or above which the frames count as perceptually identical. Sets perceptually_identical in the result.

node_isolation_path.description: Name a node in the edited scene to capture it alone, the same way viewport_capture_frame does.

resolution.description: Reserved and ignored by live capture

select_main_screen.description: Select the editor main screen this camera_identifier belongs to before capturing, then put the previous one back. An editor viewport has no size unless its main screen is showing, so without this an unattended agent cannot capture one at all. Editor sessions only.

threshold.description: How different two pixels must be to count as changed.

viewport_diff_capture.name: viewport_diff_capture
viewport_diff_capture.title: Compare two captures

viewport_set_camera_transform.description: Updates an in-scene Camera3D transform and optional field of view through the editor UndoRedo history.

camera_path.description: The camera to move. Defaults to the editor viewport's own camera.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

position.description: Where to put the camera, as {x, y, z}.

rotation_degrees.description: How to orient the camera, as {x, y, z} in degrees.

viewport_set_camera_transform.name: viewport_set_camera_transform
viewport_set_camera_transform.title: Move the editor camera

viewport_toggle_debug_draw.description: Sets editor SceneTree collision and navigation debug hints for future games run from that editor.

dry_run.description: Return a non-mutating change preview instead of executing.

wireframe.description: Always false: Godot exposes no supported live wireframe control, so the field is retained and only false is accepted. There is no second value.

viewport_toggle_debug_draw.name: viewport_toggle_debug_draw
viewport_toggle_debug_draw.title: Switch the debug draw mode
